findings: components[1].sound[1]: The Baxter–Sagart comparison lists Qing’s OC *[s.r̥]ˤeŋ and 請’s OC *[tsʰ]eŋʔ, but the table also gives 請’s distinct qíng reading as MC dzjeng, OC *m-tsʰeŋ. The article’s text presents the qǐng reading as a historical sound relationship without clarifying which 請 reading the phonetic analysis supports. Qualify the comparison as compatible with a sound relationship but not proof of the phonetic role, and state that the table records distinct 請 readings; cite X-92142940f567130d988e and X-05d1e6d031ea2259b6ec. The component’s existing modern Mandarin comparison can remain.

learner.components[1].text: “Baxter–Sagart reconstructions also show a historical sound relationship” overstates what the cited comparison establishes: the same table records two distinct 請 readings and does not by itself prove the graph’s phonetic role. Replace with a brief explanation that Qing and the qǐng reading of 請 are historically comparable in that reconstruction, while the table also records another reading; cite X-92142940f567130d988e and X-05d1e6d031ea2259b6ec.
